programme.title: Adventure All Stars
programme.desc: Margaret River is a small town south of Perth in western Australia, known for its wineries, beaches migratory whales and coastal adventures. Stretching between 2 lighthouses north and south of the town, the region fringes the limestone caves and sea cliffs of Leeuwin-Naturaliste National Park. For over 50,000 years the Margaret River Region has supported one of the world’s longest, unbroken human occupations, resulting in an immensely deep connection to the land. Natural beauty, abundance of space, fine wine and fresh coastal air make this episode a must-watch.

programme.title: New Zealand From Above
programme.desc: An aerial journey over New Zealand from the deep south of the South Island to the northern tip of the North Island. We discover the landscapes and meet New Zealanders who talk about their work, interests, and culture.

programme.title: Authentic Escapes
programme.desc: In this episode of Authentic Escapes, Sandra McLemore journeys deep into the heart of Upper Egypt—a land of ancient temples, royal tombs, and stories that have shaped civilizations. Sailing the Nile on a luxury cruise, Sandra explores legendary sites like Karnak, Abu Simbel, the Valley of the Kings, and the colorful Nubian villages near Aswan. Along the way, she shares powerful stories of queens like Hatshepsut, marvels at vibrant hieroglyphics in Seti I’s tomb, and sails silently on a traditional felucca. From spice markets to sacred temples, viewers experience the magic of Egypt through immersive storytelling and practical travel tips. Sandra offers advice on what to wear, how to stay safe, and why Egypt is a destination best explored with a professional planner. This episode is a feast of history, culture, and connection—inviting travelers to see if Egypt deserves a top spot on their travel bucket list.

programme.title: Brent Owens Unwraps Mauritius
programme.desc: Brent looks back on his time in Mauritius. Everything he's learnt, the laughs, the people, the food. Co-existence amongst the Indian, African, European and Chinese locals has led to a sharing of cultures and values, giving the Mauritians a great sense of national pride and Brent can feel it. An island commonly associated with coconuts and cocktails is proven to be so much deeper and after being welcomed into homes, sacred places of worship and given family cooking secrets, Brent is left feeling like he is part of the Mauritian family.

programme.title: Isles of the Queen
programme.desc: The rocks that make up the treeless landscape of the Shetland Islands are some of the oldest rock formations in the world. Three seas flow together here, making the waters treacherous and unpredicatble, but the island's stunning wildlife remains largely untouched.

programme.title: Isles of the Queen
programme.desc: The Isle of Man lies in the midst of the Irish Sea between Ireland and England. Officially, it belongs to the Queen, yet it has its own laws and its own currency. Its crest is the 'three legs' that symbolise its resilient people. The island holds a fascinating history of Viking settlement.

programme.title: Isles of the Queen
programme.desc: Only 25 km from the French coast lies the Channel Island of Jersey. Town names like St. Helier are reminders of its Norman ancestry. It has one of the most the most extreme tidal ranges in the world, and we will meet the Lighthouse Warden, who lives in the lighthouse that has a history of keeping pirates and smugglers off the island.

programme.title: Isles of the Queen
programme.desc: Turquoise seas, picturesque countryside, secluded coves: the Scilly Isles are Britain's sunny paradise. The mild climate allows beautiful exotic plants, even palm trees, to thrive on here. There are 140 islands, and their coves and beaches are popular with the Royals.

programme.title: Isles of the Queen
programme.desc: In the north west of Scotland stretches the island chain of the Outer Hebrides. A barren and foresaken landscape, although there are no trees, its beauty is capitvating. Fertile marshland and rocky scapes make for a harsh but wild environment, which the Queen has come to love as a holiday spot.

programme.title: Isles of the Queen
programme.desc: The Orkney Islands lie just off the North Coast of Scotland. The 70 islands are surrounded by the Atlantic and the North Sea. The landscape is made up of lush hills; steep cliffs arise in the south. Only 21,000 people live here, but there are plenty more sheep and cattle.

programme.title: Adventure All Stars
programme.desc: Darwin is the capital of Australia’s Northern Territory and a former frontier outpost. It’s also a gateway to the massive Kakadu National Park. Darwin attracts travellers from all around the globe looking to experience its outdoor tropical lifestyle. If balmy nights, colourful characters and outdoor adventures are on your bucket list, you’ll want to visit Darwin – just like our All Stars!

programme.title: Adventure All Stars
programme.desc: Located in the Northern Rivers region of New South Wales, Australia, The Tweed is adjacent to the border with Queensland. Here, nature is more thana backdrop, it’s a source of inspiration: from tropical landscapes, ancient rainforests, and world-class adventures. The Tweed is a place where sparkling seaside villages, riverside towns and hinterland hamlets create endless holiday experiences. Once you discover this place, it’s hard to forget.

programme.title: Adventure All Stars
programme.desc: Marlborough is a region of New Zealand, at the northeastern tip of the South Island. It’s well known for Marlborough Sounds, an extensive network of coastal waterways, peninsulas and islands. This area also boasts some of the world’s best walking tracks, taking in coastal forest, coves, inlets, and spectacular skyline ridges. Marlborough’s diverse landscapes – from valleys of vines to sheltered waterways – offers the perfect destination for a week of unrivalled fun and adventure.

programme.title: Adventure All Stars
programme.desc: Brisbane, capital of Queensland, is a large city on the Brisbane River. This stunning sunshine capital has no shortage of bucket list items, and our All Stars certainly ticked off a few. During this trip we also got to experience Brisbane backyard, with Moreton Bay’s tropical islands on the city’s doorstep, including beautiful North Stradbroke. Add to this a dynamic cultural precinct, abundant wildlife and easy access adventure destinations like the Gold Coast and Great Barrier Reef, and you’ve got a destination you can’t say no to.

programme.title: Adventure All Stars
programme.desc: The Sapphire Coast is located approximately halfway between Melbourne and Sydney and just three hours from Canberra, located on the far south coast of New South Wales. The roll call of magnificence is almost endless in this gem-like stretch of coast, the most southerly in the state. Discover some of the world’s best whale watching, oysters plucked straight from pristine waters, beaches where yours will be the only footprints, immense tracts of national parks and serene ocean pools. Has a coastline ever been better named?

programme.title: The Neighborhood with Nicole
programme.desc: We discover Franklin, TN also known to its locals for being voted as best small town in TN. Adventure starts our day, with a thrilling and beautiful ride showcasing the town views in a hot air balloon ride. From there we explore the history of downtown Franklin and end the day with some amazing southern cuisine.

programme.title: Toque 12
programme.desc: Phillip joins old friend, Ryan Clift, chef-owner of the newly located Tippling Club, number 23 on the San Pellegrino Asia’s 50 Best Restaurants List and known for it’s modern gastronomy and specialty cocktails.
